what_its_for: Isopropyl alcohol is used to clean and disinfect the skin before injections, minor cuts, scrapes, or small wounds. It helps kill germs and bacteria on the skin to lower the chance of infection. It is for use on the skin only and should never be swallowed.
how_to_take: For skin use only. Wet a cotton ball, gauze pad, or alcohol wipe with the solution. Gently wipe the area of skin you want to clean. Let the skin air dry completely before any injection or procedure. Do not rub hard. Never apply to deep wounds, burns, or large areas of broken skin. Never swallow this product.
dosing: Use as needed to clean small areas of skin. For wound cleaning, apply a small amount to a cotton ball or swab and gently wipe the affected area once or twice. There is no set dose schedule since this is used as needed for skin cleaning. Do not use more than needed.
missed_dose: Isopropyl alcohol is used on an as-needed basis, so there is no regular dosing schedule to miss. Simply use it when you need to clean or disinfect a small area of skin.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use to prevent evaporation. Keep away from heat, open flames, and sparks because isopropyl alcohol is highly flammable. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not swallow isopropyl alcohol — it is poisonous if ingested. Do not inhale large amounts of fumes. Keep away from open flames, sparks, and cigarettes as it is very flammable. Do not use in the eyes, ears, or nose. Do not use on large open wounds, deep cuts, or serious burns. Do not use near newborn babies' skin without medical guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help right away if isopropyl alcohol is accidentally swallowed — call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Also contact your doctor if the skin area you cleaned becomes more red, swollen, warm, or starts to drain pus, as this may be a sign of infection. Seek help if you develop a rash or allergic reaction after use.
when_it_works: Isopropyl alcohol works very quickly — it kills most germs on the skin within about 15 to 30 seconds. Always let the area air dry completely (about 30 seconds to 1 minute) before an injection or procedure for best results.
special_populations: Children: Use with adult supervision only. Keep out of reach of children. Pregnancy/Breastfeeding: Occasional skin use is generally considered safe, but avoid using over large areas of skin. Elderly: Safe for general skin use; take care with fragile or thin skin. Do not use on premature infants without specific medical guidance.
